A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mGeNTE resource and corpus-construction pipeline. Text, tables, figures and v3 Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and a changed title. v1 contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original corpus statistics, word-frequency analyses, annotator agreement and measurements of variation among translators' neutralizations (Section 3). These qualify as empirical data analyses even though model evaluation is explicitly deferred.

after.justification: v3 reports original translation and source-label evaluations, evaluator validation against human annotations, prompt and shot analyses, and context-attribution experiments, alongside corpus analyses (Sections 3–6; Appendices B–C).

M1.justification: v1 describes corpus construction without a model inference pipeline. v3 adds structured generation of a source-category label followed by its translation, using conversational demonstrations and constrained decoding, plus an adapted multilingual LLM judge (Section 4, Figure 2, Appendix B). These introduce substantive processing procedures while largely retaining the corpus-curation approach.

E1.justification: v3 adds English–Greek to the retained English–Italian/Spanish/German coverage, expanding the corpus from 4,500 to 6,000 triplets and introducing a lower-resource target with a distinct script. It also conducts model evaluations of source categorization and gendered/neutral translation. The Europarl domain and Set-G/Set-N distinction are retained.

E2.justification: v1 has no evaluated model comparisons. v3 compares Llama 3.1 8B, Llama 3.3 70B, Qwen2.5 72B, Gemma 2 9B and Phi-4 14B, with five additional models evaluated during screening (Appendix B.3). It also compares Qwen2.5 72B and GPT-4o as evaluators against human annotations (Table 5).

E3.justification: v3 introduces four prompt configurations, four-shot demonstrations excluded from evaluation, preliminary zero-/two-/four-shot comparisons, and explicit output-format controls. Evaluation adds source-label accuracy, xCOMET, GNT judgments, label–translation coherence and human validation of the judge (Section 4; Appendix B). These constitute a new evaluation design beyond v1's corpus analyses.

E4.justification: v3 adds ablations of system instructions and neutralization guidelines, shot-count and extraction-error analyses, and tests of label–translation coherence. Section 6 and Appendix C further analyze which context components contribute to classification versus translation using AttnLRP. These investigate model behavior absent from v1.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports mean ± standard deviation across prompt configurations (Table 6) and displays performance variability with error bars (Figure 3). This is limited descriptive variability reporting; neither version supplies a repeated-seed or significance-testing protocol.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive model and attribution results without corresponding v1 model scores. For example, Qwen2.5 72B with G+S achieves Set-N GNT accuracy of 0.75 for German and 0.46 for Italian (Figure 13). Existing identical-neutralization rates also change from 10.2% to 11% for Spanish and from 9% to 9.3% for German (Section 3.3).

T1.justification: Appendix B.5 newly defines span-level attribution scores and derives the summed-logit gradient and absolute embedding–gradient dot product (Equations 1–3), followed by normalization. v1 has no corresponding mathematical development. This is a limited methodological formalization rather than a new theorem or theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: v1 principally contributes a multilingual resource for neutral translation, language modeling and rewriting. v3 additionally claims the first systematic multilingual evaluation of open LMs for GNT and establishes a recognition–generation gap, model/context effects and interpretability findings. These substantially broaden the abstract, introduction and conclusion beyond the resource contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the recognition–generation gap through different contextual reliance and suggests possible lexical overfitting in source classification. It adds substantive limitations concerning prompt/model generalization, sentence-level context, proprietary evaluation and coarse attribution. v1's limitations mainly state that model experiments remain forthcoming.

D1.justification: v3 adds checkpoint identifiers, inference libraries, temperature and precision settings, decoding constraints, hardware/runtime estimates, annotation and attribution procedures, and code/artifact access information (Appendix B). v1 mainly documents corpus construction and translator guidelines. Its explicit CC BY 4.0 license statement is omitted in v3, without establishing a license change.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around multilingual benchmarking, open-model evaluation and interpretability. Background/Table 1 compare resource coverage and evaluation support, including FairTranslate; the text contrasts its evaluation with earlier single-language studies. Section 6 adds a substantial attribution/interpretability lineage, including AttnLRP, beyond v1's inclusive-language and resource overview.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around recognizing versus producing neutrality. Separate language-background and related-work discussions are consolidated into Background, while corpus explanations are condensed and details moved to Appendix A. The title, terminology and contribution narrative also change substantially.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 1–3 are expanded, redrawn or merged into appendix Figures 8 and 20; corpus statistics and examples are reorganized across main-text and appendix tables. v3 also adds study and prompt diagrams, performance plots, ablation heatmaps and attribution visualizations, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the benchmark's demonstrated utility, completing the model evaluation explicitly deferred in v1. Multilingual comparisons, human validation of the evaluator, prompt analyses and attribution experiments establish a consequential recognition–generation gap and clarify conditions affecting GNT. Detailed implementation reporting further supports reuse. Proprietary judging and coarse attribution restricted to one model limit reproducibility and generalization, but these limitations are acknowledged and do not outweigh the substantial empirical gains.
